policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 9 Jun close (1x4 3.89, 3x6 4.00, 6x9 4.25, 9x12 4.47 vs WIBOR 3M 3.88) price roughly 60bp of NBP hikes within 12 months. The MPC held at 3.75% on 2 Jun (May CPI eased mainly on food; decisions stay data-dependent); Glapiński (3 Jun): lower May CPI cuts the hike odds, rates are high enough and there is no reason to change or even discuss them. Masłowska (9 Jun): cuts are now more likely than hikes, conditional on CPI staying below 3.5% and no escalation. May flash CPI 3.1% (29 May; 3.7% expected, -0.3% m/m on food); core 3.0% in April. The fuel VAT and excise cuts run to 15 June (extended 28 May).
policy.risk_text: The MPC turned dovish (Glapiński, 3 Jun: no reason to change or even discuss rates), so FRAs trade oil and the Iran talks; risks: renewed Gulf fighting and the fuel package ending (excise from 15 Jun) lifting CPI; long end: the 17 and 24 Jun sales and the deficit.

macro.projection_text: NBP March projection (4 Mar; data to 19 Feb, war excluded): CPI 50% bands 1.6-2.9% (2026), 1.1-3.7% (2027); central path 2.3% / 2.4% / 2.3% (2026-28), GDP 3.9% in 2026; IMF (14 Apr): 2026 CPI 3.3%; EC (21 May): GDP 3.5% in 2026; OECD (June outlook): CPI 3.7% in 2026, no cuts before Q2 2027; Fitch (8 Jun): GDP 3.3%, NBP flat at 3.75% to year-end. The July projection is the next marker.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit 7.3% of GDP (GUS EDP, 22 Apr), debt 59.7%; 2026 deficit cap PLN 271.7bn; budget deficit after April PLN 89.3bn (30.1% of the limit); the government's assumptions put the 2026 deficit at ~6.8% of GDP; EC (21 May): 6.5%, debt 64.5%; EKF consensus (2 Jun): 6.9%; 2027 budget path (9 Jun): GDP 3.1%, CPI 2.5%; windfall-tax bill (75% of margins above the 2025 level +20%) in preparation; fuel package (VAT 8%, price caps, minimum excise) to 15 June (28 May).
macro.fiscal_risk_text: 2026 needs ~56% (MoF, 29 May) financed; budget accounts PLN 208.3bn at end-May (MoF, 8 Jun); 3 Jun switch (MoF database): PLN 11.63bn sold (demand 12.84bn) vs 10.90bn bought back (PS0527 7.42bn), net +0.73bn; OK0129 4.812%, PS0731 5.269%, DS0436 5.703%; BGK priced EUR 2bn of FPC bonds (2 Jun). S&P A-/stable (affirmed 8 May); Scope A negative (15 May); Fitch A- and Moody's A2 have negative outlooks; Fitch's June forecast round (8 Jun) was not a rating action.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP held at 3.75% on 2 Jun; May CPI 3.1% y/y; Q1 GDP 3.5% y/y (second estimate). Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 9 Jun: MPC's Maslowska (Bloomberg): cuts are now more likely than hikes, conditional on CPI staying below 3.5% and no escalation. The government's 2027 macro path: GDP 3.1%, CPI 2.5%, wages 5.6%; public pay +3%, pensions at least +3.48%. Registered unemployment 5.9% as expected. POLGB yields fell 11-14bp as NBP hike pricing receded (Kurtek). EY: rates unchanged, core 3.0% in 2026. Abroad: Trump said a 'very good deal' with Iran is in the final stretch, but Iran shot down a US Apache over Hormuz and he vowed a response. Brent fell ~4% to ~$91; gold closed at $4,286, the lowest since December; UST10 4.54%, Bund 10Y 3.05%; OAT-Bund jumped to 78bp (flagged); Hungary May CPI 1.8%; ~51% for an October Fed hike, ~70% for December.

calendar.plan_text: MoF June plan (29 May): one switch on 3 Jun (settles 8 Jun; buys back DS0726, PS1026, WZ1126, OK0127, PS0527) and sale auctions on 17 and 24 Jun (PLN 6-12bn each) in OK0129, NZ0331, PS0731, DS0436 and NZ0936; no T-bills; ~56% of 2026 needs financed. 3 Jun switch (MoF database): PLN 11.63bn sold (demand 12.84bn) vs 10.90bn bought back (PS0527 7.42bn), net +0.73bn; OK0129 4.812%, PS0731 5.269%, DS0436 5.703%. BGK priced EUR 2bn of FPC bonds on 2 Jun; FPC switch on 18 Jun (buys back FPC0427).
calendar.timing_text: The Aug 2025-Feb 2026 pattern (auction-day close the cheapest point of the week) comes from a rally regime; March's sell-off broke it and April's auction days cheapened on average. Remaining June operations: 17 Jun, 24 Jun. Next MPC in July, with the NBP projection: a hold is expected.

facts.core_text: Regime: talks stalled and Gulf clashes resumed - Brent back at ~$95-98; the NBP held at 3.75% on 2 Jun while FRAs price roughly 60bp of NBP hikes; the ECB is priced for a June hike, the Fed is priced for a 2026 hike, the BoE is priced for hikes, the CNB is on hold and the MNB is on hold. Apache downed; Brent -4% to ~$91 (9 Jun).

quasi_takeaways: FPC fixed lines trade ~{lo}-{hi}bp over the POLGB curve (average {avg}bp); widest ASW {widest} at {widest_asw}bp. Same State Treasury guarantee as POLGBs.
Best pickup: {best} ({best_sp}bp vs POLGB). For buy-and-hold books the guarantee makes the pickup attractive; liquidity is the cost (Pekao became BGK market maker on 13 Nov 2025).
Supply: BGK priced EUR 2bn of FPC bonds on 2 Jun (8Y EUR 1.25bn, 15Y EUR 0.75bn; demand EUR 4.6bn); FPC switch on 18 Jun (buys back FPC0427).
Use auctions, not Catalyst: trades are small retail lots and some lines go weeks without a print.
